# roster — CLI Contributor Guide

This repo builds and ships **`@firatcand/roster`**, an npm CLI that installs/scaffolds the agent-team pattern across Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Gemini. See `README.md` for the user-facing pitch; this file is for contributors working on the CLI itself.

> **Working on Roster?** This file describes **Roster the product** — what it is, where things live, how it builds and ships.
>
> For the **Forge methodology** we use to build Roster (principles, planning workflow, branch strategy, GitHub-Issues-as-source-of-truth, worktree/PR rules), see [`.forge/CONTEXT.md`](.forge/CONTEXT.md). Keep the two sets of rules separate so they do not bleed into each other.

## Repo layout

```
src/        CLI source (TypeScript, ESM, Node ^22.18 || >=24)
  bin/      roster.ts — argv parsing, subcommand dispatch
  commands/ init.ts, (doctor.ts coming Phase 2)
  lib/      tools.ts (detection + install), paths.ts (ROSTER_ROOT, getPackageVersion)
bin/        Build output — bin/roster.js is the executable entry. Gitignored.
lib/        Build output for library exports. Gitignored.
templates/  Files copied into a user's workspace by `roster init`.
  scaffold/ Directory tree mirrored verbatim into the user's CWD.
  CLAUDE.project.template.md, env.example, gitignore-defaults.txt
skills/     Skills shipped to AI tools by `roster install`. One dir per skill.
agents/     Agent .md files shipped alongside skills (Claude Code only).
test/       Node test runner specs + smoke.sh integration test.
docs/       Public docs. docs/adr/ contains historical implementation records, not active product-spec decisions.
.forge/     Forge methodology rules + worktree harness state (not shipped).
spec/       Tracked durable product authority — BRIEF, PRD, SPEC, CONTEXT, and ephemeral decisions.
plans/      Tracked design/decomposition snapshot — GitHub owns live execution state.
```

GitHub Issues owns live task status, assignment, sequencing, and blockers. Query GitHub for routine tracker-state reads and use read-only/dry-run reconciliation. Run a non-dry `forge orchestrate reconcile --pull` only when its resulting `plans/phases.yaml` snapshot will be committed, including the one-time post-bootstrap refresh that replaces the dangling `spec_revision`.

**Shipped to npm** (verified via `npm pack --dry-run`): `bin/`, `lib/`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `templates/`, `data/`, `README.md`, `LICENSE`. This is the exact `package.json#files` allowlist; tracked `.forge/`, `spec/`, and `plans/` artifacts never ship.

## Build & verify

```bash
pnpm install         # node 22+
pnpm typecheck       # tsc --noEmit
pnpm build           # tsdown → bin/roster.js with shebang
pnpm test            # node --test on test/**/*.test.ts
pnpm smoke           # bash test/smoke.sh — pack, install, init end-to-end
pnpm perf            # bash test/perf.sh — measure install/init/doctor + tarball against SPEC budgets (dev-machine only)
pnpm test:scaffold-scripts # test/new-agent-slash-only.sh + test/audit-agent-guideline-refs.sh — exercises templates/scaffold/scripts/
npm pack --dry-run   # confirm tarball stays clean (~554 kB packed, 86 files after `pnpm build`; -2 retired v1 dreamer templates #359)
```

The Phase gate command (run before opening a PR): `pnpm typecheck && pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm test:scaffold-scripts && pnpm smoke`.

## Where things live in the CLI

- **Subcommand entry**: `src/bin/roster.ts` — hand-rolled argv parsing; subcommands `install`, `init`, `update`, `upgrade`, `doctor`, `schedule`, `review`, `skills`, `hooks`, `pending`, `migrate`, `brain`, `task`, `ops`. `--help`, `--version`, exit codes (0/1/2/3).
- **V2 workspace update**: `src/commands/update.ts` (`roster update`) preflights the sparse workspace, synchronizes only unedited generated host activation, and regenerates the deterministic `.roster/vendor-skill-map.json` from complete secret-free tool-use definitions. It never installs global vendor skills or probes host caches. Invalid/incomplete tool guidance fails before any update write. `src/lib/update-args.ts` parses `--cwd`/`--json`.
- **Host adapter contract**: `src/lib/generated-artifacts.ts#HOST_ADAPTER_LIFECYCLE_CAPABILITIES` is the single capability catalog and renderer for the host-neutral `ROSTER.md` lifecycle and thin Claude Code/Codex activation pointers. `src/lib/context-trust.ts` owns the ordered trust classes shared by generated guidance and context results. Keep lifecycle policy out of host-specific wrappers.
- **Tool detection**: `src/lib/tools.ts` — `detectTools()` checks `~/.claude/`, `~/.codex/`, `~/.gemini/`. Each `Tool` has `key`, `name`, `skillsTarget`, `agentsTarget`. Override via `ROSTER_CLAUDE_HOME` etc. for tests.
- **Install logic**: `installToTool()` in `src/lib/tools.ts` — copies `skills/*` and `agents/*.md` into the tool's config dir. Idempotent. Handles symlinks (prompts before clobber). Handles EACCES with a sudo hint.
- **Scaffold logic**: `src/commands/init.ts` — copies `templates/scaffold/**` into CWD, substitutes `{{PROJECT_NAME}}` in `CLAUDE.project.template.md`, appends gitignore-defaults idempotently.
- **Schedule schema**: `src/lib/schedule-schema.ts` — Zod-validated `scheduleEntrySchema` (name, agent, plan, cron, tool, install_mode, status). Required `status` enum is `pending-ui-install | installed`. `validateCronExpression()` for cron syntax.
- **Schedule install (Claude)**: `src/lib/schedule-install.ts` — `installClaudeSchedule()` renders `.roster/schedule-specs/<name>.claude.fields.md` (markdown, NOT JSON — Spike 2) and upserts `roster/<function>/schedules.yaml` atomically. UI hand-off only; tracked under [anthropics/claude-code#41364](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/41364).
- **Schedule install (Codex)**: `src/lib/codex-install.ts` — `installCodexSchedule()` with two modes: `ui-handoff` (default; renders `<name>.codex.fields.md` for the Codex desktop app) and `via-cron` (`--via cron`; renders a hardened crontab line wrapped by `env -i`, installed via `src/lib/codex-cron.ts` marker-block upsert). All entries include a `subscription_attestation` block (auth_mode/env_policy/codex_home) verified by `src/lib/codex-preflight.ts`. Marker ids are function-scoped (`<function>/<schedule>`); the pre-#323 BARE `<schedule>` marker is adopted only when BOTH guards hold — the name is registered by exactly one function in the workspace (`functionsRegisteringSchedule` → `legacyMarkerIsAmbiguous`) AND the block's own rendered channel path proves that function (`legacyMarkerOwnedBy`). install/remove refuse an ambiguous block; doctor reports it as `ambiguous-legacy-marker`.
- **Shared YAML helpers**: `src/lib/schedule-yaml.ts` — `atomicWriteFile`, `readExistingSchedulesDoc`, `upsertEntryInDoc`. The upsert refuses to overwrite an existing entry with a different `tool` value to prevent silent same-name cross-tool collisions.
- **Schedule commands**: `src/commands/schedule.ts` — `executeScheduleValidate()` and `executeScheduleInstall()`. The install command preflights `--cloud-routine` (not-yet-implemented), Linux + `--tool claude` (no Desktop Scheduled Tasks on Linux), `--via cron` (codex-only; refused on Windows), `--tool codex` default mode (refused on Linux — no Codex Desktop).
- **Failure observability (ROS-42)**: `src/lib/cron-exit-log.ts` reads sibling `logs/cron/<name>.exit` / `.events.jsonl` files written by the `renderCronLine` wrap (create-only under `set -C` noclobber after an `rm -f` — a planted symlink at the exit path is never followed; a failed create means NO exit file, which the stale path surfaces). Every read of an agent-writable evidence/registry/correlation file — `<fireId>.exit`, `<fireId>.run-id` (list AND the create-only conflict arbitration), `roster/<fn>/state.md`, `roster/<fn>/schedules.yaml` (ALL readers: schedule list/resolve, the install/remove upsert in `schedule-yaml.ts`, `schedule-validate.ts`, doctor's entry listing), and `roster/<fn>/pending/*.md` — goes through the leaf module `src/lib/evidence-read.ts#readEvidenceFileSync` (O_NOFOLLOW + O_NONBLOCK + fstat regular-file + read-to-EOF under a `maxBytes+1` bound; `schedule-state.ts` re-exports it, and the local ops ledger imports it directly — the split exists so the ledger can share one hardened reader without an import cycle), so a planted FIFO/symlink/oversized file is reported as malformed by each caller's own error path and can never block or divert a reader, and a concurrent append to `state.md` can never truncate a complete line into a false STALE. A symlinked `schedules.yaml` is refused, not followed. `O_NOFOLLOW` covers only a path's FINAL component, so every DIRECTORY walk over the workspace tree (`scanPending`, `listFunctionDirs`/`loadSchedules`/`readScheduleEntries`, `findScheduleFiles`, `listExitRecords`/`listScheduleRuns`, doctor's entry listing) and every mutation (`atomicWriteFile`, `readExistingSchedulesDoc`, `approveItem`/`rejectItem`) is confined through ONE primitive in `src/lib/workspace-path.ts` — `resolveConfinedPath(path, boundary)`, which walks EVERY path component strictly below the boundary with `lstat` and refuses ANY symlink component **regardless of where it points**, plus a realpath belt that can only ever add a refusal. Earlier rounds used realpath CONTAINMENT (accept if the resolved chain lands inside the workspace), which by construction blessed an IN-WORKSPACE symlinked ancestor: `roster/gtm/pending/acknowledged -> <ws>/archive/acks` suppressed a real failed fire, and `roster/ops -> gtm` aliased two function identities onto one registry. Both of the primitive's inputs are ABSOLUTE by contract (`assertAbsolutePath`): it used to resolve a RELATIVE target beneath a RELATIVE boundary, so `--cwd repo` (process cwd `/parent`) made a caller's already-prefixed `repo/roster/…` become `/parent/repo/repo/roster/…` — confinement inspected a phantom path while every caller afterwards opened the real one (`run list` reported no runs, `run start` replaced the ledger's producer identity, and a symlinked component on the REAL path was never walked). Every `--cwd` parse site now normalizes with `resolve()` and a relative input THROWS instead of being re-prefixed; the one caller-authored workspace-RELATIVE input (pending front-matter `target_on_approve`) goes through the explicit `resolveWorkspaceRelativePath`. `targetWithinWorkspace`, `confinedWorkspaceDir`, `confinedFunctionDir`/`resolveFunctionDir`, `functionDirWithinRoster` and `confinedProbeSync` are all thin wrappers over that primitive; `ancestorsConfined` is the flavor for readers that own their final component through `O_NOFOLLOW` (`readWorkspaceEvidenceFileSync` folds a refusal into the existing `malformed` taxonomy as `outside-workspace`, so a symlinked evidence FILE keeps its precise `not-a-regular-file` reason). So a symlinked `roster/gtm` or `roster/gtm/pending` can never divert a read, a rewrite, or an unlink — to another repository or to another directory of the same workspace. The workspace is not the innermost boundary: a **function name is a caller-supplied path segment** (`--function`, the `<function>/<agent>` positional), and `../archive` — or an in-workspace `roster/gtm -> ../archive` — satisfies the workspace check while leaving the registry, so `schedule remove --function ../archive` rewrote a sibling `schedules.yaml`. Function names are now validated by ONE strict kebab rule at every argument boundary (`workspace-path.ts#isFunctionName`, used by `schedule-args`, `run-args`, `review-args`) and every resolved function directory is confined beneath `<workspace>/roster/` — `confinedFunctionDir` for reads (`listFunctionDirs`/`loadSchedules`/`readScheduleEntries`/`findScheduleFiles`/`scanPending`/`pending-sync`/`review`) and `functionDirWithinRoster` for the create-on-first-use write path (`assertFunctionDirWithinRoster`, shared by both installers). Existence probes over agent-writable paths (the `acknowledged/` sentinels, both pending destinations, the approve target) use the tri-state `confinedProbeSync` instead of `existsSync`, so a symlinked `acknowledged/` can no longer classify a failed fire as acknowledged and silently suppress its decision item. `src/lib/schedule-state.ts#detectStale` answers "is the agent self-report older than expected next-fire + grace?". `src/lib/pending-sync.ts` synthesizes `roster/<fn>/pending/error-<id>.md` items from non-zero `.exit` + STALE — idempotent via `sha1(scheduleName + signalKey).slice(0,8)`. `src/commands/pending-sync.ts` is the CLI; `src/lib/doctor-scheduling-drift.ts#auditStaleFires` is the doctor cross-reference. `templates/hooks/banner.sh` v3 invokes `roster pending sync --silent` (with `timeout 5`) on SessionStart before counting items, so failures from between sessions surface in the next chat; the banner reads `⚠ You have N unread decision(s) awaiting — run /inbox`.
- **HITL review / inbox (ROS-132)**: `roster review` is the engine. `src/lib/pending-apply.ts` holds the shared apply logic (`approveItem`/`rejectItem`, both re-confining the item path before rename/unlink; the boundary itself — `targetWithinWorkspace`/`confinedWorkspaceDir`/`workspaceRelative` — lives in the leaf module `src/lib/workspace-path.ts`) plus `computeItemId` (`sha1(function/filename).slice(0,8)`) and `resolveItemBySelector` (path-then-id). `roster review --json` lists items with an `id`; `--approve`/`--reject <id|path>` apply one headlessly (before the TTY guard). `skills/inbox/SKILL.md` is the cross-tool `/inbox` front door — a chat-driven router over those verbs (no TTY). "Unread" is a rebrand of the pending count; no read/seen state.
- **Task state machine (ROS-147, v1.5.0)**: `src/lib/tasks/` — `machine.ts` (pure canonical transition table: `ready → claimed → active → review → done`, `blocked`/`cancelled` branches), `context.ts` (tracker.yaml load, `deriveCurrentState` incl. assigned-Ready→claimed overlay, `planVerb` collapse over unmapped stages, `resolveSelector`), `tracker-schema.ts` (Zod config), `setup.ts` (board introspection wizard), `adapters/` (`types.ts` generic `TrackerAdapter`, `notion.ts` v1 impl — sole layer touching Notion). Verbs + reports live in `src/commands/task.ts` (`applyVerb`, `composeReport` = stable flat `list`, `composeDigest` = `status` stage digest + attention). `skills/tasks/SKILL.md` is the `/tasks` chat front door (never writes the tracker directly). Interactive only — no autonomous pickup.
- **Expert-route drift guard (ROS-129)**: `src/lib/founder-skills/expert-routes.ts` — `parseExpertRoutes` + the `KNOWN_FOUNDER_SKILLS` allowlist (+ `BUILTIN_SKILL_EXCEPTIONS`, e.g. `frontend-design`). Guard pair: `test/expert-routes.test.ts` pins `templates/scaffold/*/EXPERT.md` routes to the allowlist (hermetic; `ROSTER_NETWORK_SMOKE=1` adds a live GitHub-catalog verify), and `src/lib/doctor-expert-routes.ts#auditExpertRoutes` warns in `roster doctor` when a workspace EXPERT route isn't covered by `founder-skills.yaml` (`expert_routes` in `--json`) — warning-only, never flips the exit code; not-applicable without (or with an invalid) manifest, drift.ts owns the fail-loud path.
- **Ops persistence boundary (#318)**: `src/lib/persistence/` — `contracts.ts` (store interfaces + error taxonomy + `committed|queued` write outcomes), `config-schema.ts` (`roster/persistence.yaml`, credential-free), `local/` (append-only JSONL ledger + stores; the READ side is confined by `confinedLedgerDir` — the read-only sibling of `ensureOwnedDir` over the same component-wise no-follow primitive, creating nothing and repairing no mode — so `scan`/`meta`/`readLedgerMeta` refuse a symlinked `.roster/ops/<workspaceId>` instead of reconstructing (and locking, recovering, sealing) a FOREIGN ledger tree; `meta.json`, the seal sidecars, `persistence.yaml` and the setup journal are read through the hardened bounded reader, and the lock + segment reads open `O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK` with an fstat regular-file re-proof; create-once publication is `link(2)` → `O_CREAT|O_EXCL`-at-the-final-name → **refuse**, never a replacing rename, and `getArtifact`/`head` share one descriptor-verified (`O_NOFOLLOW` + regular-file) digest-checked blob read), `outbox.ts` (durable spool: fold-over-events, backlog barrier, poison parking; the spool + checkpoint READS are confined too — `spool/` and the outbox namespace dir go through `confinedLedgerDir`, spooled bytes through the descriptor-verified `readRegularFileSync` (digest-bounded, the artifact/blob policy) and `outbox/checkpoint.json` through the hardened bounded reader at the 64 KiB sidecar cap, so a symlinked `spool/` can neither divert nor chmod a foreign file and a FIFO at `checkpoint.json` can no longer hang a drain after its remote commits), `postgres/` (`binding.ts` strict 1:1 workspace↔DB stamp verified per connection, `roles.ts` least-privilege gate, `stores.ts`), `objects.ts` (dedicated-bucket create-only store + `roster-workspace.json` marker + `listPrefix` for repair/doctor), `resolve.ts` (`resolveOpsBackend(cwd)` — the seam #320/#321 consume; legacy/local/postgres-s3/degraded/setup-incomplete; `resolveObjectAdmin` = the list-capable admin/read object resolver repair/doctor use), `setup.ts` + `setup-journal.ts` (roll-forward `roster ops setup`), `capabilities.ts` (per-component version negotiation). CLI: `src/commands/ops.ts` + `src/lib/ops-args.ts`. Schemas ship from `data/ops/schema/{hitl,roster_ops}/`. Env: `ROSTER_OPS_URL`/`ROSTER_OPS_ADMIN_URL` (dedicated) or the brain pair (brain reuse). Protocol reference: `docs/adr/0004-operations-ledger-contracts.md`.
- **Run + artifact ledger (#323)**: `src/commands/run.ts` (`roster run`) + `src/lib/run-args.ts` — verbs `start`/`end` (source=`cli`), `event` (generic; refuses lifecycle/tool-result/report/artifact-declared via `assertGenericEventKind`, requires `--correlation-id`), `report` (source=`agent`, `--file`/`--stdin` + a **128 KiB PORTABLE raw cap** enforced BY the read via `lib/bounded-read.ts` — a multi-GiB file is refused from its stat, an unbounded pipe is abandoned at cap+1, and a file that GROWS past the cap mid-read reports `size: null` rather than its stale pre-read stat — stored through the sanitizer; 128 KiB is derived from the local ledger's 1 MiB **record** limit minus worst-case 6× JSON escaping + the sanitized projection + the envelope, so the advertised cap is achievable end-to-end on every backend), `declare-artifact` (`--digest`+`--file` internal via `putArtifact(meta,bytes,decl)` with `--role produced|used`, or `--external provider:id --url` via `putExternal`), `show` (`composeRun` over `getRun`+`getByRun`+`head` blob resolver), `list` (`--task`/`--agent`/`--limit`), `doctor`, `repair --fill-version-ids` (both admin verbs assert `runs.doctor`/`runs.repair` capabilities BEFORE resolving admin creds or issuing SQL — a v1 backend gets a `VersionSkewError`, never a raw SQL error). Pure model: `run-events.ts` (sealed provenance + source trust taxonomy `host-attested`/`cli`/`agent`/`unverified`), `run-compose.ts` (`composeRun` — lifecycle promoted only from trusted sources, duration derived at read), `sanitize-index.ts` (write-time redaction → the `run_index`/`artifact_index` views), `artifact-declarations.ts` (identity split: blob vs declaration; id covers `role`). Repair: `run-repair.ts` — `diagnoseRunLedger` is read-only (incl. `declaration-version-unverified`: a declaration still unverified while its blob records a version); `fillVersionIds` is the SOLE updater of `object_version_id`/`version_state` (admin creds; runtime holds no UPDATE grant). An artifact spooled during an outage marks its declaration version-PENDING, and ordered drain materialization derives `version_state='verified'` from the committed blob row — a healed outage self-converges; the direct path's committed-ROW verdict is never re-derived. Migration `data/ops/schema/roster_ops/002_run_ledger.sql` (v2). All verbs resolve via `resolveOpsBackend`, close the PG pool in `finally`, and are opt-in — legacy workspaces without `persistence.yaml` are unaffected. The bin entry flushes stdout/stderr before `process.exit` so a large `--json` payload is never truncated into invalid JSON on a pipe.
- **HITL state machine (#319)**: `src/lib/persistence/hitl-machine.ts` is the ONE shared machine both backends route through — closed `EDITORIAL_ACTIONS` allowlist (unknown action ⇒ `execution`, fail-safe), the length-prefixed `requestKeyOf`/`targetHashOf`/`packetHashOf` framing the SQL reproduces byte-for-byte (Node↔SQL vectors), `TRANSITIONS`/`canDecide`/`canAuthorizeExecution`/`validateApproval`/`planSubmission`/`deriveRequestState`. Around it: `hitl-store.ts` (pre-backend layer — server-side content-hash verification, >8 KiB offload through #323's object port, expiry clamp, decision normalization, deterministic `systemExpiryId`), `hitl-sweep.ts` (bounded + throttled bookkeeping), `hitl-local-migrate.ts` + `hitl-local-records.ts` (local v1→v2), migration `data/ops/schema/hitl/002_state_machine.sql` (component v2, capability `state-machine`). **Identity** is the request GROUP: `request_key = sha256(functionName, action, target)`, `request_id = sha256(workspaceId, request_key)` — content is deliberately NOT in the key, so a revision is version N+1 of the same group; `generation`/`version` are allocated synchronously under the per-group advisory lock (`hashtext(request_key) # 1212765260` — `0x4849544C`, deliberately not a schema-migration key since the mask IS the lock id when `hashtext()` returns 0 — / the local `hitl` namespace lock) and `(request_id, generation, version)` is the decision + FK identity. **The DB owns canonical identity**: the fill trigger RECOMPUTES `action_kind`/`request_key`/`target_hash`/`canonicalization_version` from the row's own inputs on every insert — filling what a writer omitted, REFUSING what it asserted differently (a caller that asserts a derivation it did not compute is a bug or an attack: asserting `action_kind='editorial'` for an execution action bought an expiry-free approval that `authoritative`/`canAuthorizeExecution` accepted) — and derives `id = sha256(workspace_id, request_key)`, RE-KEYING a v1-shaped/legacy-drain insert onto it (old value → `legacy_id`) or REFUSING a v2-shaped insert whose id disagrees with its own key. The fill trigger also validates ALLOCATION, not only derivation — under the SAME per-group advisory lock (both groups in sorted key order for a supersession row, re-entrant inside a store txn) it refuses an insert that extends a group whose current head is superseded (permanent closure at the DB level), claims a `(generation, version)` that is not the legal next step (no gaps, no reuse, no revision in a sealed generation, no G+1 while G is open — sealing judged by the DURABLE terminal decision, never the clock, since every path that opens G+1 materializes the expired head's decision first), names a supersession target that is not the current, not-already-superseded head of the group it replaces OR one that is effectively expired with no durable terminal decision, or REVISES an effectively-expired head. Those last two are judged by the CLOCK on purpose, and together with the decision-judged G+1 rule they close an expired generation: a raw `G1/V2` over an expired-but-unswept head became the actionable head and HID V1 from every future sweep, so its expiry was never recorded at all — while G+1 stays decision-judged so a deadline crossing mid-write cannot refuse a legal allocation. It costs the store nothing (`sealed` already counts the clock, so no store path ever plans a revision of an expired head), both rules are monotone (a decision is never un-recorded, a deadline never un-passes), and the one window left — a deadline crossed between plan and insert — is the same synchronous `ConflictError` the decision trigger's expiry-direction check raises. Like the decisions trigger it lock-then-reads, so it carries the SAME contract and RAISEs above READ COMMITTED: a snapshot taken before the lock reads the group as it was before a concurrent supersession and allocates a head beside it. The anti-join is written once as `hitl.head_superseded` and called by the projection, the decision trigger and this gate. Only `expectedHead`/`intent` and `packet_hash` stay application-enforced (the DB cannot know what a caller observed, and cannot reproduce JS canonical JSON). The key being derived is what makes the id check meaningful, so one `request_key` can never own two groups and no separate `UNIQUE (request_key)` is needed. `canonicalization_version` is likewise derived-and-verified per CHANNEL — inline: `payload->'body'` must be a JSON string whose sha256 equals `content_hash` (an EMPTY body hashing to `sha256('')` counts, matching the TS conversion); payload_ref: `payload_ref->>'digest'` must equal `content_hash`, the bytes being re-hashed against it by every reader that materializes them — because without it a plain INSERT stored `body='benign text'` beside `content_hash=sha256('executable text')` at version 1 and, once approved, was `authoritative` and `validateApproval`-authorized for the packet the approver never saw. The check is EQUALITY with the derived value in both directions (`1` iff verified, else `0`), so an understated 0 over verified content and a forward-compatible `2` the schema cannot verify are refused exactly like an overstated 1 — the TS side ships one canonicalization version, and a second is a schema change that teaches the trigger to derive it. Version 0 stays the legacy exemption (D8: never authoritative). **One functionName rule everywhere**: functionName has no column of its own, so `hitl.function_name()` (fill trigger + backfill + the PG list/count FILTER), `functionNameOf`/`identityFieldsOf` (PG projection), the local projection at read and the local v1→v2 conversion all apply the same normalization — anything not a NON-EMPTY string is `unknown`, inline channel first then `payload_ref.meta`; comparing the RAW payload value in the PG filter hid a migrated `functionName: 5`/`''`/absent row from the very `unknown` query its own envelope advertised. **Optimistic concurrency**: `expectedHead` is REQUIRED and carries `{generation, version, packetHash, sealed}` — `sealed` is mandatory because a terminal decision changes nothing else about a head, so without it a submission composed against an open request would open G+1 behind an approval the caller never saw; `null` = 'no history at all' (also honored idempotently when the head is an OPEN byte-identical packet — an at-least-once retry). `replaces` validates BOTH expected heads and is idempotent over the (packet, supersession) PAIR, so it never reports success with the source still authoritative; it also materializes BOTH closed heads' owed expiries — the destination's generation boundary AND the SOURCE's — inside the same two-lock transaction/batch, in sorted `request_key` order, before the destination row lands, because a supersession pointer closes the source permanently and an un-materialized expiry under it could never be written by anyone afterwards. **A superseded group is CLOSED**: the supersession pointer lives on the DESTINATION row, so being replaced leaves the source head's fingerprint byte-identical (same generation/version/packetHash/sealed) and `expectedHead` alone can never detect it — so the SAME anti-join that denies authority is read inside the group lock during PLANNING (`HitlObservedHead.superseded`) and refuses every WRITING plan (`revise`/`open-generation`) with `superseded-head`, on both backends and on the pre-#319 spool drain; the source side of `replaces` is refused the same way. Without it a caller that observed S before `replaces(S → D)` submitted its unchanged fingerprint and minted an S head no supersession row points at — authoritative alongside D, two live approvals for one replaced decision. Only a byte-identical packet against an open head stays idempotent (it writes nothing) — and because a `replaces` still owes its supersession link, such a no-write DESTINATION plan is UPGRADED to a writing revision when the head does not already record that link, so closure is re-checked against the FINAL plan: `A→B`, then `B→C`, then `X→B` with B's own fingerprint and packet committed a B v2 that C's pointer at B v1 does not cover. `hitl-store.ts#finalizeSubmissionPlan` is the ONE place a plan's kind may change after `planSubmission` returned, and it owns both the upgrade and the re-check. Same closure downstream: a superseded head leaves the DEFAULT actionable list/count workset (`deriveRequestState().actionable` / `NOT s.superseded` in the PG filter; an explicit `status` filter still reaches it — that is history, not the queue) and is never an expiry candidate, `insertSystemExpiry` reporting `conflict` on both backends rather than writing (local) or raising (PG, whose decision trigger refuses every decision on a superseded version). The **packet hash** covers every approval-VISIBLE field including `title`, `originRunId`, `originTaskId`, `requestingAgent` (canonicalization version stays 1 — nothing has ever shipped a packet hash). **Sealed generations**: any terminal decision seals a generation and a later same-key submission opens G+1 (an independent approval) — but **sealing ≠ authority**: `canAuthorizeExecution` is the HIGHEST generation's current, unsuperseded, unexpired, `canonicalization_version > 0` head with effective status `approved`, so an approved TERMINAL head IS authoritative (the normal approve-then-execute path) and authority never falls back to an older generation. Insert-only, no UPDATE grant anywhere: supersession is derived from row existence (`supersedes_*` + anti-join), and the admin-owned BEFORE INSERT triggers on `hitl.decisions` and `hitl.requests` (advisory-lock FIRST, READ COMMITTED-only — both RAISE under a higher isolation whose snapshot predates the lock — `clock_timestamp()` for every expiry comparison) make the invariants true against a raw runtime INSERT. Expiry is enforced sweep-INDEPENDENTLY: `effective_status` drops an expired request out of authority and out of the actionable count before any sweep runs; the sweep only materializes the durable `expired` decision (deterministic id ⇒ concurrent sweeps converge; on PG it is stamped with the DB clock read inside the locked txn — the same clock that decided eligibility — so a skewed app clock can never record an expiry at a moment the request had not yet expired; PG USER decisions read that same `hitl.now_ms()` after the group lock for their prevalidation and stamp, so an app clock running ahead cannot refuse a decision the DB considers decidable), and `hitl.expiry` in `persistence.yaml` (24h default, clamped to 1h…7d with a warning on `HitlWriteOutcome.warnings`) is the policy — RESOLVED on PG against the DB clock under the group lock, with the packet re-sealed around the result (`resealExpiry`), because `expiresAt` is packet-visible and every expiry CONSUMER reads `hitl.now_ms()`: resolving it on the application clock made a 24h request BORN expired when the app ran two days behind the database, and pushed the expiry past the DB-relative 7-day maximum when it ran ten days ahead. **Live-store-only** (owner decision 6): `createRequest`/`replaces`/`appendDecision` all require the authoritative store, the ENTIRE `hitl` namespace is refused at `LocalOutbox.enqueue` (structural, not by convention), degraded HITL reads throw and honor no `allowPartial`, and for a database-less workspace the local JSONL ledger IS the live store (physical record id is composite so a revision never dedups against its base). Migration: PG partitions legacy generations at terminal boundaries and re-keys `id` (old value kept in `legacy_id`), refusing an ambiguous history in preflight — every preflight/partition/remap join is keyed by the FULL v1 identity `(workspace_id, id, request_version)`, since v1's unique allows several versions per legacy id. Local converts under the SAME `hitl/.lock` v1 writers respect, in BOUNDED CHUNKS (one compound record would blow the ledger's 1 MiB limit and make a large history unmigratable), with a durable CONVERTING marker + epoch revalidation making a re-run idempotent; the marker is also a FORMAT FENCE the ledger's append primitive enforces (`local/format-fence.ts`), so a v1 writer that resolved before the conversion cannot append a v1-format record AFTER it and have the v2 projection ignore it forever. Each converted version carries its legacy `createdAt` as an observation, so the projection reports the ORIGINAL creation time (parity with the PG backfill, which leaves `created_at` alone). A legacy row with an absent or non-string body converts to `body: null`, not `''` — postgres keeps the v1 payload jsonb verbatim and projects a non-string body as null, so the same row must not report two different bodies in an audit. Because a conversion chunk is ONE compound envelope, its children share a ledger seq: local pagination orders by the tuple `(seq, pos)` (`pos` = index within the envelope, assigned by `expandLedgerRecords`, carried on `Cursor.committedPos`) — a scalar seq cursor made every batch sibling but one permanently unreachable. Both backends anchor HITL pagination on the GROUP's creation position (the lowest seq its versions hold), never the head's — a head moves on every revision, so projecting the latest head and then applying `seq <= watermark` dropped a request revised mid-traversal out of the whole listing. CLI verbs are #320. Protocol: `docs/adr/0004-operations-ledger-contracts.md` §HITL state machine.

## Adding a new AI-tool target

1. Add the tool's config-dir constant to `src/lib/tools.ts` (e.g., `~/.somewhere/skills/`).
2. Add a `Tool` entry to `detectTools()` returning the key + name + targets.
3. Extend `installToTool()` to handle that tool's layout (skills-only vs skills+agents).
4. Add a test case in `test/install.test.ts` exercising the new target.
5. Update `README.md` install matrix.

## Code conventions

- TypeScript, ESM, strict mode. No CommonJS.
- File names: lowercase kebab-case.
- Prefer hand-rolled argv parsing over commander/yargs to keep tarball small.
- No comments unless behavior is non-obvious. No docstrings.

(Build conventions — GitHub issue numbers in commits/branches, phase gates, worktree/PR rules, never auto-commit — live in [`.forge/CONTEXT.md`](.forge/CONTEXT.md). Roadmap is `docs/roadmap.md`; work items tracked in [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/firatcand/roster/issues).)

## Dogfooding

There is no in-repo agent-team workspace anymore. To exercise the workspace pattern shipped by `roster init` (`/sdr`, `/chief-of-staff`, `/dreamer`, etc.), scaffold a workspace outside this repo with `roster init` and report regressions back here. The shipped scaffold is exercised in-CI by `pnpm smoke` (`roster init` into a tmpdir) and `pnpm test:scaffold-scripts` (the `new-agent.sh --slash-only` and `audit-agent.sh` guideline-refs regression suites).

## When in doubt

Start here, then check [`.forge/CONTEXT.md`](.forge/CONTEXT.md) for build methodology and tracker/phase rules, then `README.md` and `docs/HOWTO.md`. If a CLI convention isn't clear, ask before guessing — this is going on npm and inconsistent UX propagates to everyone who installs it.
